demonstrated_findings: Maximum lag follows a 17.6170999766 ms housekeeping interval containing 13.6826999951 ms protected-state fsync, then an 84.2608999810 ms adapter step. The step contains 55.3924000124 ms observation update, including 48.4491999960 ms protected-event fsync. These selected fsync rows have zero recorded host thread/process CPU; the adapter reports 15.625 ms CPU.

The 23-24 s bad window crosses adapter step 23.9327335000-24.0181328000 s. Its protected-event fsync lasts 51.8510999973 ms and crosses wall 24 s. Interpolation gives sim 23.9335687045 at wall24 and 25.0 at wall25, producing RTF 0.93356870449 then catch-up 1.06643129551. Both violate unchanged bounds.

Other substantial synchronous waits occur in public event fsync, registry fsync, public-state fsync and SQLite commits/execute. The longest adapter step contains a54.4674 ms SQLite commit followed by14.1669 ms protected-event fsync. A SQLite mode-only change does not address the actual maximum-lag and bad-window protected-journal paths.

All six automatic-collector policies and resource gates pass. No cyclic collection overlaps measured physics; stock-1 has one generation0 collection after the terminal/restore boundary. Memory is below soft/hard ceilings and stock-1 maximum sampling gap153.6501 ms remains below200 ms.
No atomic-replace retry occurred in any run. Stock-1 evaluator max1.456 ms and recorder lock-acquire max0.0397 ms do not explain its failed intervals.

Stock-1 has33 fresh timing gaps above40 ms:30 end before25 s,1 in25-30 s,1 in30-35 s and1 in50-55 s. The next five runs have smaller journal maxima. This is temporal concentration, not causal evidence for startup/cache warmup.
unresolved: The nested phases localize delay to synchronous API intervals, not to a specific storage-device/driver/filter/host-process cause. Zero CPU is quantized host CPU accounting and includes blocking/descheduling; it is not a kernel I/O trace.

No retained OS disk queue, device service-time, file-system/filter or scheduler trace identifies why the API calls delayed. External work, power settings, warmup and cache state must not be asserted as causes.

Bounded top-row retention omits shorter phases and some repeated intervals; nested parent/child durations overlap and must not be summed. The23-24 s affected interval is directly retained, but a complete per-operation latency distribution cannot be reconstructed from selected phase rows.

recommendation.proportionate_next_direction: Investigate the shared synchronous durability path with a bounded prospective, non-physics, source-bound reproduction of protected/public event and atomic-state fsync plus FULL SQLite operations on the actual intended storage path, paired with OS I/O and scheduling attribution if available. Declare fixed workload/order/limits before execution. Use that evidence to choose and qualify a material host/storage repair; do not claim a repair is identified by this diagnosis.
recommendation.conditional_repair_scope: A storage-path/device or interfering-workload correction is proportionate only after its contribution is measured. Preserve write/flush/fsync/replace order, commit-before-visible semantics, quotas, timing thresholds and original evidence. Any off-thread durable writer or batching design would change synchronization/failure semantics and needs a separate design/parity/failure qualification; it is not authorized or validated here.
recommendation.PERSIST: No adoption. Earlier feasibility passed mechanics but did not establish host-tail benefit; this run independently places both failed boundaries in protected journal fsync outside SQLite.
recommendation.requalification: Only after a material repair, create a new frozen revision and run the complete prospective qualification gates. Preserve this native003 invalid result without replacement or softened thresholds.
